title: Financial advisor
tagline: Learn to guide clients from first meeting to a signed financial plan with clarity and trust.
setting: Conversations happen in a private office, on video calls, and at kitchen tables where clients keep their statements.

scenarios.label: First discovery meeting
scenarios.desc: A new client sits down with statements spread out, unsure what a planner actually does.
scenarios.setup: You are a certified financial advisor. The client opens with: I have accounts everywhere and no idea if any of it fits together.
scenarios.objective: Agree on a planning scope and book the data gathering session.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:15 am, late morning light through vertical blinds

scenarios.label: Plan presentation
scenarios.desc: You walk the client through a draft plan that shows a shortfall they did not expect.
scenarios.setup: You are a certified financial advisor. The client opens with: I thought I was on track, why does this say I fall short at eighty?
scenarios.skills: Framing trade offs, visual storytelling, calm reassurance
scenarios.objective: Get client approval on the core assumptions and move to implementation steps.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 3:40 pm, golden hour light warming the table

scenarios.label: Annual implementation review
scenarios.desc: A year later the client questions fees and wants to shift strategy after a market dip.
scenarios.setup: You are a certified financial advisor. The client opens with: My statement shows high fees and the portfolio dropped, so why stay the course?
scenarios.skills: Fee transparency, rebalancing discipline, regulatory compliance
scenarios.objective: Confirm the fee structure, explain the rebalance, and re-sign the ongoing service agreement.
scenarios.moment: Monday 9:00 am, overcast sky with cool fluorescent glow

buyers.angle: Wants the bottom line in five minutes and doubts a planner adds value.
Afraid of mistakes, needs every term explained in plain language.
Scrutinizes every assumption and pushes back on projected returns.
Resists diversification and questions why fees apply to held shares.

buyers.role: long term client facing market drop
buyers.angle: Sees a paper loss and ties it to advisory cost, ready to leave.

objections: Why should I pay you when a robo advisor charges a fraction?
I don’t want to lock money away I might need next year
Your projected returns look optimistic compared to the last decade
The fee schedule is confusing, what am I actually paying for?
My CPA already handles my taxes, why add another layer?
I prefer to pick my own funds, I have beaten the market before
What happens if you leave the firm or we stop working together?
Can you guarantee I will not run out of money in retirement?

rubric.label: Discovery depth
rubric.what: Uncovers goals, fears, and all assets before recommending anything.

rubric.label: Risk alignment
rubric.what: Matches portfolio risk to the client’s true capacity for loss.

rubric.label: Fee transparency
rubric.what: Explains every cost in dollars and basis points with no jargon.

rubric.label: Fiduciary clarity
rubric.what: States the advisor’s legal duty and any conflicts in plain language.

rubric.label: Scenario modeling
rubric.what: Shows best, base, and stress cases with live numbers the client can test.

rubric.label: Implementation discipline
rubric.what: Keeps the client on the agreed rebalance schedule through market noise.

pitfalls: Recommending products before the fact find is complete.
Blurring advisory fees with product commissions in the client’s mind.
Implying guaranteed returns or downside protection that does not exist.
line: Selling financial plans as a financial advisor
